text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 2.6% today, recovering some ground after a sharp 4-day sell-off that had knocked the stock down nearly 8% from its mid-September peak. The bounce came as oil prices ticked up on September 24th amid reports of potential negotiations around the Hormuz Strait — a critical chokepoint for global crude supplies — and as the refining sector digested mixed signals on diesel policy. US crude sitting at $96.41 per barrel and refineries running at 94% capacity suggest the company still has decent operational economics, even if recent volatility has been pronounced.

The stock's recovery also reflects some relief from the diesel export ban threat that had weighed heavily over the prior days. While a ban would initially support refinery margins by keeping more fuel domestic, industry warnings about long-term price spikes and production cuts appear to have sparked a reassessment — the move higher today suggests traders are pricing in either a softer policy outcome or simply a reversal of overdone pessimism from the previous session.
